## Why This Is Asked

Tests ability to translate a feature into a practical CBA using on-device ML, privacy, and rollout considerations.

## Key Concepts

- Local model size and latency
- Energy and memory constraints
- Telemetry vs privacy trade-offs
- Rollout and break-even planning
- Compliance and opt-in considerations

- How would you handle drift in user input and model retraining on-device?
- What metrics would trigger a roll-back or pause in rollout?

## Why This Is Asked

- CRDT state growth and memory budget

```javascript
function mergeCRDT(local, remote) {

}
```

- What metrics and experiments would you run to validate the break-even model?

## Why This Is Asked
This question probes practical cost modeling for edge privacy features with multi-language policy governance and federated updates. It tests ability to quantify resource budgets, update economics, and regulatory risk in a real-world scenario.

## Key Concepts
- On-device ML budgets: RAM, CPU, energy per inference
- Federated policy updates and security
- Multi-language policy governance and compliance
- Evaluation metrics: FP/FN, precision/recall, uplift in safety
- Break-even and go/no-go criteria

## Code Example
```javascript
function estimateInferenceCost(modelMB, opsPerInference, batteryWh){
  // simplistic proxy for energy cost per inference
  const energy = (modelMB * 0.6) + (opsPerInference * 0.0005);
  return energy; // in mWh
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would FP/FN targets vary across languages and policies?
- How do you handle policy drift and secure updates?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests the ability to manage risk in live ML-style deployments, ensuring data integrity and latency goals while using feature flags and controlled rollouts.

## Key Concepts
- Canary deployments and feature flags
- Drift detection and rollback strategies
- Observability, alerts, and guardrails
- Auditability and versioning of models/artifacts

## Code Example
```javascript
// Pseudo drift check sketch
function driftOk(liveDist, offlineDist, thresh){
  const kl = klDiv(liveDist, offlineDist);
  return kl < thresh;
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you choose drift thresholds? Why different for users vs. admins?
- How would you structure pre-release validation and rollback testing before full reintroduction?
